benchmarks: own case studies (FutureShorelines WebGIS legacy-code refactor; COVID-19 infodemic-mapping cartographic-reliability rubric per Mooney & Juhasz 2020); no standard public benchmark
fallos_mitigaciones: The paper's premise IS 5 LLM failure modes (C1 long-context degradation, C2 cross-session forgetting, C3 stochasticity, C4 instruction-following failure, C5 adaptation rigidity via costly fine-tuning). Mitigated by the dual-helix's two axes: Knowledge Externalization persists facts outside the ephemeral attention window and restores project context via a standardized initialization protocol (fixes C1/C2); Behavioral Enforcement makes protocol compliance mandatory rather than advisory (fixes C4), unlike RAG whose 'retrieved text serves merely as context that the model may probabilistically ignore as task complexity grows'; the self-learning cycle persists newly discovered patterns as auditable graph nodes without retraining (fixes C5).
cita: Guan et al. (2026). A Dual-Helix Governance Approach Towards Reliable Agentic AI for WebGIS Development.
notes: S3.2 3-track KG substrate: Track1(Knowledge)=facts/patterns nodes (mem_tipos=SEMANTICA), Track3(Skills)=validated reproducible workflows (PROCEDIMENTAL); every node is a version-controlled JSON document with parent links -> representacion=GRAFO, retrieval=GRAFO (agent 'traverses the hierarchical relationships', queries KG for 'step-specific constraints'). S3.4 5-step self-learning cycle (Discovery->Structuring->Linking->Validation->Persistence, Fig4) -> operaciones=WRITE;ADMISION(schema-check+human Agent-Builder review before persisting); trigger=DISCRECIONAL-LLM(agent decides when it 'discovers' a concept)+CHECKPOINT(persistence at session/step boundaries). S4.4 Table4: KG grew 28->126 nodes (+350%) during FutureShorelines refactor, 98 nodes created autonomously and human-reviewed -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI (auditable/version-controlled/reversible, reviewed to avoid 'redundancy or hallucinations'). S4.5 controlled 3-condition experiment (Fig7/8): dynamic KG-retrieval (Condition C, dual-helix) vs static full-prompt (B) vs unguided (A), same info/model(gpt-5.2), 5 trials each -> directly measures retrieval-STRUCTURE utility: C halves variance (sigma=0.36 vs 0.79) and wins Rule-Compliance E5 by +27.7pp (1.66 vs 1.30) despite a SMALLER per-step prompt (~1400 vs ~4000 tokens) -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. S5 5-condition COVID-19 cartographic ablation (Table5/Fig10): Full Dual-Helix 8.33 best; removing Skills(E)->6.33 (largest drop, near-baseline 6.22), Behaviors(D)->7.22, Knowledge(C)->8.00 (smallest) -> ABLATION ranks Skills>Behaviors>Knowledge for this task. S3.3 role separation: Agent Builder(meta-level, can itself be an LLM agent per COVID case study)+Domain Expert(task-level) SHARE the KG substrate -> multiagente=SI. S3.4/S4.5 'phase memory' + session-specific KG-State track step-by-step plan/discovery progress explicitly INJECTED forward into subsequent steps (Fig9b: 4->17 entries) -> plan_estado=SI. Table3: SLOC -49%, cyclomatic complexity -51%, maintainability +7pts, JSHint warnings -98% (code-quality OTRA metrics) -> metricas=EXITO(compliance scores)+OTRA(code-quality). Cross-session persistence (addressing C2) + mandatory behavioral protocols = literally what travels between sessions -> handoff=CONTENIDO;CONTRATO. F confirms F_screening (WRITE;PROCEDIMENTAL) + adds RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, FIDELIDAD, MULTIAGENTE, DOCS-VERSIONADO (version-controlled/auditable/reversible framing throughout).

fallos_mitigaciones: Prior LLM-based code-optimization approaches operate purely at the instance level (one-shot rewriting or retrieved exemplars) and 'do not explicitly distill reusable optimization knowledge', repeatedly re-deriving the same fixes -- mitigated by mining mechanism-level Operator/Meta Skills instead of instance pairs. Skill-library fragmentation/redundancy from clustering is mitigated by merging highly similar skill summaries at a TF-IDF cosine threshold of 0.8 followed by a conservative LLM merge pass, keeping the final library compact.
cita: Wang et al. (2026). EffiSkill: Agent Skill Based Automated Code Efficiency Optimization.
notes: S3.2 Stage I (offline): trace extraction (ProblemBrief/SlowAudit/FastAudit/DeltaSummary) from 900+900 paired slow/fast programs -> signature abstraction -> hybrid TF-IDF+dense-embedding (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) clustering -> Operator Skills distilled per cluster + Meta Skills as procedural controllers; merge threshold 0.8 cosine + LLM merge pass -> operaciones=WRITE;CONSOLIDACION, representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS (skill cards, Fig2: metadata+body fields), retrieval=EMBEDDINGS. Stage II (S3.3, execution-free): Diagnose->RetrieveSkills(3 candidate sets)->ComposePlans(2-3 plans)->GenerateCandidates, NO runtime execution feedback in the loop. Table2 RQ2 ablation (S5.2): 'w/o Retrieval' (generate directly from diagnosis, skip skill retrieval) vs 'w/ Random Skills' (uniformly-sampled skills replace retrieved ones) vs 'w/o Multi Plans' -> Random-Skills ablation is a textbook retrieval-precision test -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO; paper concludes 'relevant skill retrieval improves alignment with optimization bottlenecks'. Table1 (RQ1/RQ3): EffiSkill beats Instruction/CoT/RAG/FasterPy/SBLLM/EffiCoder baselines by 3.69-12.52pp OPT@k across GPT-5-mini/Qwen3-Coder-30B, Python+C++ (cross-language RQ3 consistency). Single offline-mined static library reused at inference, no online agent-to-agent sharing studied -> multiagente=NO. F confirms F_screening (PROCEDIMENTAL;WRITE) + adds RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, CONSOLIDACION (merge-threshold dedup).

benchmarks: GAIA, ALFWorld, WebShop, TravelPlanner, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, AIME24, AIME25 (8 benchmarks, 6 task categories)
fallos_mitigaciones: Creating new tools/agents from scratch without experience guidance causes 'non-replicable success and repeated errors' (motivating gap vs pure capability-centric baselines like Alita/AutoAgents) -- mitigated by conditioning asset creation on retrieved Experience Memory (Eq6). Also, 'a correct answer does not guarantee robust underlying assets' -- mitigated by a Self-Correction Loop: newly created assets must pass an LLM-synthesized unit-test Valid() gate (Eq8) before persisting to Asset Memory; failed validation triggers Improve() revision + regenerated tests until it passes (Eq8-9).
cita: Cheng et al. (2026). Mem2Evolve: Towards Self-Evolving Agents via Co-Evolutionary Capability Expansion and Experience Distillation.
notes: S3.1 Dual-Memory: Asset Memory MA=Bagt(cup;Btool (expert-agent specs <role,expertise,suggestions,tools> + MCP tool records <name,func-desc,code,docs>, PROCEDIMENTAL) + Experience Memory ME=Eagt(cup;Etool (lessons <title,desc,use-cases,content> distilled from success/failure trajectories, EPISODICA) -> representacion=HIBRIDA (structured records+code+text). S3.2 forward inference: Recruitment Function Gamma(si) via sim(si,MA)>=delta (EMBEDDINGS retrieval) picks reuse-vs-create; Creation conditions on Retrieve(si,Etool)+web search (Eq6) -> retrieval=EMBEDDINGS. S3.3 backward evolution: Judge()=LLM-as-judge produces (rt,ct) (trigger=DISCRECIONAL-LLM) after each task (trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA pipeline stage); Asset Memory Evolution gates new assets through Valid(mnew,ct) unit-test verification before MA<-MA U {mfinal} (Eq8-9, operaciones=ADMISION;ACTUALIZACION) -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI (explicit pre-persistence correctness verification). Experience Memory Evolution: Reflection(tau_t,rt,ct) distills BOTH Success-Generalization and Failure-Diagnosis lessons, merged via ME<-ME U {enew} (Eq10-11, CONSOLIDACION). Table3 RQ1 ablation: w/o Tool Creation -10.28pp (largest), w/o Expert-Agent-Creation -1.72pp, w/o Agent-Memory -4.73pp, w/o Tool-Memory -3.13pp. Table4 RQ2 (S5.2): Experience-Guided vs w/o-Exp.-Guide asset creation directly measured -> First-Pass-Validity +56.0% relative on GAIA, Avg.Improve.Iter down to -68.4% on AIME -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (explicit read-utility measurement). Table2: Mem2Evolve avg Pass@1 70.24% vs strongest capability-baseline Alita+6.46%, experience-baseline AFLOW+11.80%, naive-LLM+18.53%; RQ4 explicitly claims 'effective memory reuse in cross-task settings' -> alcance=PROYECTO. Experience Memory guides MULTIPLE recruited expert agents ('guiding specific expert agents in handling complex tasks') sharing the same pool -> multiagente=SI. F confirms F_screening (CONSOLIDACION;PROCEDIMENTAL) + adds WRITE, RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, MULTIAGENTE, FIDELIDAD.

benchmarks: DriftBench (own, 880 pairs: 174 controlled drifts + 107 real-world drifts + 599 negative controls, from 49 SWE-Skills-Bench source skills)
fallos_mitigaciones: The entire paper addresses skill staleness: 'skills silently decay as the external services, packages, APIs, and configurations they reference evolve' (APIs migrate, packages deprecate, URLs move, auth mechanisms change, 8 drift types S3). Naive contract-free monitoring over-alerts (40% FPR from probing every changed value, including incidental mentions like documentation links). Mitigated by SKILLGUARD's role-bearing contract extraction: only OPERATIONAL-role assumptions are validated (raises ZERO false alarms over 599 no-drift/hard-negative cases, Wilson 95% CI [0,0.6]%), and violated contracts localize repair (one-round success 10%->78% vs unlocalized 'the skill is stale' prompting).
cita: Fan et al. (2026). Skill Drift Is Contract Violation: Proactive Maintenance for LLM Agent Skill Libraries.
notes: S4: skill document S -> deterministic regex pass across 15 pattern families (URLs/versions/imports/API-paths/auth/Docker/env-vars/etc, retrieval=GREP-ARCHIVOS) finds candidate mentions; a semantic pass labels each as OPERATIONAL vs INCIDENTAL (role decision) forming contract records C(S)={(type,role,value,evidence)} -> operaciones=ACTUALIZACION (repair rewrites stale skill content once a contract is violated; no new-skill creation/write pipeline is studied here, skills pre-exist from SWE-Skills-Bench). S4.2 contract-drift matching predicate is type-gated+token-overlap based, applied ONLY to OPERATIONAL-labeled records -> this precision-first ordering (role-filter BEFORE probing) is the paper's central mechanism, distinct from a retrieval-utility axis, so mide_lectura=NO (the axis measured is content VALIDITY/staleness, not read-precision for a downstream task) -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI is the dominant facet instead. S5.1 Table2: 100% precision / up to 76% recall (best backbone) on known-drift verification across 5 LLM backbones; ZERO false positives over 599 negative controls (vs CI-probes 40% FPR, Dependabot-style 10% FPR). S5.2 pre-registered LIVE study over 49 real skills: 86% conservative precision, 55% recall, 7% FPR (2 apparent FPs later confirmed genuine drift). S5.3 repair: contract-localized repair 78% one-round success (p<1e-5 vs no-localization's 10%) using ~10K tokens/skill vs ~18K for 3-round Self-refine (COSTO-TOKENS;ITERACION=round count). S6 sensitivity ablation: expanding regex families 7->15 raises real-world recall 45%->78% at 0% FPR. F confirms F_screening (FIDELIDAD;PROCEDIMENTAL) + adds DOCS-VERSIONADO (drift = pinned-dependency/version staleness in skill documents, the paper's core framing).

benchmarks: ALFWorld (229 curated SkillsBench skills + synthetic degraded variants, 9 library scales 200-2000 skills)
fallos_mitigaciones: 'Skill technical debt': persistent library-level defects (redundancy, missing validation, interface drift, stale implementations) that don't break a single skill locally but harm future retrieval/composition/execution as the library grows -- task-time repair fixes one episode while the underlying defect remains. Mitigated by a 5-dimension health diagnosis (Utility/Redundancy/Compatibility/Failure-Risk/Validation-Gap, Eq4) feeding typed maintenance actions: merge (collapses redundancy-edge duplicates), repair (rewrites failing operations from execution feedback), retire (removes obsolete/failing skills), add_validator (fills validation gaps), add_adapter (fixes type-incompatible dependency edges).
cita: Song et al. (2026). SkillOps: Managing LLM Agent Skill Libraries as Self-Maintaining Software Ecosystems.
notes: S2-3: each skill = typed Skill Contract (P,O,A,V,F); library=Hierarchical Skill Ecosystem Graph (HSEG) with dep/comp/red/alt typed edges -> representacion=GRAFO, mem_tipos=PROCEDIMENTAL. Task-Time Loop (Alg.1): skill matching r(s,tau)=lambda*BM25+(1-lambda)*semantic (Eq1, retrieval=RANKING;EMBEDDINGS), then dependency+compatibility-constrained graph stitching (retrieval=GRAFO also), validator/adapter insertion, local repair on failure. Library-Time Loop (Alg.2, Fig1 orange): 'mines skill contracts from execution logs' (WRITE) -> 5-dim health diagnosis + optional CGPD risk-propagation over dep edges (Eq5) -> typed actions merge(CONSOLIDACION)/repair(ACTUALIZACION)/retire(OLVIDO)/add_validator(ADMISION, fills Validation-Gap G(s)=1[Vs=empty])/add_adapter; trigger gated by DeltaH<Theta_maint threshold (PRESUPUESTO) after each task (EVENTO-DETERMINISTA). H3 ablation (Table5): removing Task-Time Loop drops SR 79.5%->15.7% (largest), removing Library-Time Loop drops to 71.9%, graph-level ablations to 64.6%/72.2% -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (isolates retrieval/graph-stitching value directly). H1 (Table1): SkillOps_Full 79.5% SR on ALFWorld vs strongest baseline LLM_Skill_Planner 70.6% (+8.9pp), zero std across seeds. V4 plug-in (Table2): consistently helps retrieval-heavy baselines (+2.90pp Hybrid, +1.00pp BM25, +1.12pp Dense) when swapped into their unchanged code -- direct evidence maintenance improves READ quality. H2 (Table4): SkillOps stays ~79-80% SR as library scales 200->2000 with rising synthetic degradation density (15%->90%), while task-time-only baselines degrade sharply -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI. V2 (Table3, S6.4): nearly-zero library-time LLM cost (rule-based), task-time tokens mostly neutral/negative (24/35 cells decrease) -> COSTO-TOKENS. F confirms F_screening (PROCEDIMENTAL;FIDELIDAD) + adds WRITE, RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, CONSOLIDACION, COSTO.

benchmarks: MBPP+ hard-100 (Claude Opus 4.7, 100 rounds x 3 seeds, own reproducible-trigger + 8-ablation protocol)
fallos_mitigaciones: The paper's entire subject IS a memory failure mode it names 'library drift': unbounded skill accumulation without outcome-driven lifecycle management causes retrieval degradation, false-positive/stale injections, and performance stagnation-or-collapse below the no-skill baseline (silent: 'end-task metrics decline gradually with no explicit error signal'). Mitigated by the Ratchet recipe: outcome-driven retirement (Nmin=100 trials + contribution threshold tau=0.10, formal non-divergence guarantee Prop.1), a bounded active-cap (C=50, forces eviction of lowest-contribution skill), and a meta-skill authoring prior (reduces harmful/redundant skill births at the source, -43% of Default's gain when ablated, the single most valuable component). Critically documents a NEGATIVE result: harsh/premature retirement (A4, Nmin=20) is WORSE than no governance at all (-0.019, below the no-skill floor) -- governance itself can actively harm when calibrated on insufficient evidence (Hoeffding epsilon~0.44 at Nmin=20).
cita: Zhang et al. (2026). Library Drift: Diagnosing and Fixing a Silent Failure Mode in Self-Evolving LLM Skill Libraries.
notes: S3-5, Fig1 'Ratchet' loop: persistent append-only Skill Bank(ACTIVE+DEPRECATED, never deletes raw log)+Meta-Skill Bank(one ACTIVE authoring prior)+Evidence Log(capsules+verdicts) -> representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS, mem_tipos=PROCEDIMENTAL. Router picks skill via tf-idf-union-embed similarity (S6.3 A2 ablation description) -> retrieval=RANKING;EMBEDDINGS. Synthesizer clusters>=3 failures sharing a canonical pattern into ONE new skill (operaciones=WRITE;CONSOLIDACION); Curator retires if per-skill contribution ĉ(s)=(succ-fail)/trials < -tau after Nmin trials (OLVIDO, EVENTO-DETERMINISTA-gated) and enforces the bounded cap C=50 (PRESUPUESTO); Meta-Synth rewrites the meta-skill every N rounds (ACTUALIZACION, CHECKPOINT-triggered, A8 ablation). S4 trace-level diagnostics (per-skill contribution score Eq2, HELPED/HURT/NEUTRAL/INAPPLICABLE attribution verdicts, router-engagement%) are explicitly designed to measure retrieval/injection utility BEFORE it reaches aggregate pass@1 -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO is the paper's central diagnostic axis. Table1/Fig2 (8 ablations, 3 seeds): Default lifts pass@1 0.258->0.584 late-window (+0.328); A1(no injection, floor)+0.002; A4(harsh retirement)-0.019 BELOW floor (explicit NEGATIVO governance-harm finding, consistent across all 3 seeds -0.005/-0.027/-0.025); A5/A6(no dedup) slightly EXCEED Default, showing the meta-skill subsumes explicit deduplication. S6.4: Default uses ~14.5k LLM calls/100 rounds (COSTO-TOKENS, +43% vs no-skill A1) and 6.5h wall time vs A1's 2.3h (LATENCIA). Explicit staleness framing throughout ('stale skill injected into the solver prompt actively misleads', 'silent injection harm') -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI. Single frozen LLM plays ALL pipeline roles (Router/Solver/Grader/Critic/Synthesizer/Curator/Meta-Synth), not separate persistent cooperating agents -> multiagente=NO. F confirms F_screening (CONSOLIDACION;PROCEDIMENTAL) + adds NEGATIVO (A4 governance-harm), WRITE, RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, FIDELIDAD, COSTO.
